holidays.name: National Pink Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate all things pink, from flamingos and bubblegum to rosé and cotton candy. Folks are encouraged to wear pink, eat pink foods, and decorate with the cheerful color.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance popularized through novelty-holiday calendars and social media, celebrating the color's associations with joy, kindness, and playfulness.
holidays.funFact: The 'Baker-Miller Pink' shade was once used to paint holding cells in some prisons in the late 1970s because researchers believed it could calm aggression, though later studies found the effect to be short-lived.

holidays.name: Let It Go Day
holidays.description: A day to release grudges, clutter, worries, and perfectionism. Think of it as permission to stop stressing, whether you belt the Frozen song in the shower or simply toss out that junk drawer.
holidays.origin: An unofficial self-care observance that encourages people to let go of what no longer serves them. It's a popular theme on wellness and novelty-holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: The song 'Let It Go' from Disney's Frozen won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 2014 and has been translated into more than 40 languages for the film's international releases.

holidays.name: International Widows Day
holidays.description: A United Nations observance that shines a light on the poverty, discrimination, and legal injustice many widows face around the world. It is a serious awareness day amid the quirkier ones on this date.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly officially designated June 23 as International Widows Day in 2010, following years of advocacy by the Loomba Foundation, which first marked the day in 2005.
holidays.funFact: The date was chosen to honor the anniversary of the day Raj Loomba's mother became a widow in 1954, and the Loomba Foundation was created in her memory.

holidays.name: United Nations Public Service Day
holidays.description: A day to applaud the civil servants who keep the world running, from the people who fix the roads and process permits to those who answer the phones at city hall.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly designated June 23 as UN Public Service Day in 2002 to recognize the value and virtue of public service to the community.
holidays.funFact: The UN Public Service Awards, given on this day, recognize innovative government programs, and winners have included projects ranging from digital citizen portals to community health initiatives.

holidays.name: Typewriter Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the clacking, dinging, ink-ribbon marvel that powered a century of writing. Typewriter fans celebrate by banging out letters, poems, and the occasional ill-advised novel.
holidays.origin: The date honors the anniversary of Christopher Latham Sholes receiving a patent for his typewriter on June 23, 1868.
holidays.funFact: The QWERTY keyboard layout is often said to have been designed to keep typebars from jamming, which is why common letter pairs were separated, and that layout still dominates the phone in your pocket today.
